text.p: British retailer Kingfisher Plc said Wednesday that a housing market upturn and a revival of consumer confidence spurred recovery at its B&Q home decorating chain and helped first-half pre-tax profits jump 47 percent to 109.6 million pounds ($169.9 million).
B&Q's turnaround was driven by improved market conditions, increased market share and better operationing performance.
At B&Q, Kingfisher's largest unit in terms of sales and profits, profits rose 48 percent to 47 million pounds ($73 million) from 31.8 million pounds ($49.3 million). Sales were up nearly 16 percent.

As the market leader in home improvement retailing in Britain, B&Q had been struggling in a depressed market, where overcapacity brought cut-throat competition from rivals like Sainsbury's Homebase and Texas Homecare and Boots Co. Plc's Do It All.
Chief Executive Sir Geoffrey Mulcahy said the British do-it-yourself market grew by about 4 or 5 percent in the first six months of the year.

Comet, Kingfisher's electricals retailer posted a loss of 3 million pounds ($4.7 million) vs. a loss of 8.7 million pounds ($13.5 million) a year ago. The company's Woolworths division returned to profit of 4.6 million pounds ($7.1 million), after a 900,000 pound ($1.4 million) loss the year before.

Profits at French electricals retailer Darty were 42.5 million pounds ($65.9 million), up from 40.0 million pounds ($62.0 million). Superdrug profits rose by 9.3 percent to 16.4 million pounds ($25.4 million).
